newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds unchanged ahead of rate announcement.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds unchanged ahead of rate announcement.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged in quiet trading on Thursday as the market went into a holding pattern ahead of the Bank of Israel interest rate announcement on Monday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.01 pct at 103.03
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct at 102.11
Volume was low at 125 million shekels.
"Overall the market was very stable because investors are waiting for the interest rate decision," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.
A trader at IBI Investment House, echoing the market consensus, said her company was predicting a rate cut of 0.3 percentage points or less from the current 14.2 percent.
"CPI-linked short bonds rose slightly while long ones declined. Beside that nothing happened," she said.

Dollar-linked bonds were also stable as the shekel remained almost unchanged against the dollar in trading today. In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3510 shekels against 3.3520 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
